issues.title: Docs: Update storage requirement from 1TB to 2TB+ for mainnet sync
issues.body_excerpt:
# Rationale

The current recommendation of `1TB` in `README.md` is outdated and insufficient for post-Merge mainnet operation.

A complete mainnet setup requires both an Execution Client (Geth) and a Consensus Client (e.g., Prysm, Lighthouse). Combined with historical data (`ancient` storage) and execution state, the required disk space exceeds 1.5TB–2TB immediately. Recommending 1TB causes new node operators to experience disk-full errors, severe I/O bottlenecks, and OOM crashes during initial sync.

# Implementation

Update `README.md` to reflect actual operating requirements:

**Minimum:** High-performance SSD with at least **2TB** of free space.
**Recommended:** High-performance NVMe SSD with **2TB–4TB** of space for long-term growth and maintenance headroom.

````
`validateHeader` in `tests/block_test_util.go` compares `baseFeePerGas` with `reflect.DeepEqual` (line 334, as of aa1f2fcf5), while every other `*big.Int` field in the same function uses `Cmp` — `Number` at line 301, `Difficulty` at line 322.

json "0x0"  -> abs nil = false

issues.title: eth_simulateV1 with `validation: true` skips the EIP-7825 transaction gas-limit check
issues.body_excerpt:
## Summary

The documentation states:

> When true, the `eth_simulateV1` does all the validation that a normal EVM would do, except contract sender and signature checks.

On an Osaka, pre-Amsterdam chain, a normal transaction whose gas limit exceeds the EIP-7825 cap is rejected, but the same call succeeds through `eth_simulateV1` with `validation: true` when the simulated block gas limit is raised.

The simulator passes the `validation` option into its nonce-check behavior, but `TransactionArgs.ToMessage` still sets `SkipTransactionChecks: true` unconditionally. This bypasses the EIP-7825 transaction gas-limit check as well as the documented contract-sender exception.

Documentation: <https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/interacting-with-geth/rpc/ns-eth#eth-simulate-v1>

## System information

- Runtime reproduction: Geth `1.17.5-unstable`, commit `81ab8b594ebe0f672450779d4b308f3f33191828`
- Platform: macOS arm64, Go `1.26.3`
````

````
### System information

### Description

When JSON-RPC transaction args include both an EIP-7702 `authorizationList` and legacy `gasPrice`, `internal/ethapi.TransactionArgs.ToTransaction()` silently serializes the request as a legacy transaction.

case args.AuthorizationList != nil || defaultType == types.SetCodeTxType:
````

````
## Problem

The hand-written JSON marshalers for `BlobAndProofListV1` and `BlobAndProofListV2` always emit a JSON array. When the list is nil, this encodes as `[]`.
````

````
System information

  CL client & version: N/A
  OS & Version: N/A

  Expected behaviour

  When a peer sends a GetTrieNodes request containing a compact-encoded path longer than 33 bytes, the server should reject or skip it, or even disconnect the peer because it sent a malformed message. A compact-encoded path of 33 bytes represents the maximum trie depth of 64 nibbles (Keccak256 = 32 bytes = 64 nibbles).   In ServiceGetTrieNodesQuery (eth/protocols/snap/handlers.go), path bytes are passed directly to accTrie.GetNode(accKey), which calls compactToHex(path) (trie/encoding.go) and traverses the trie  without validating the path length.   1. Resource waste: compactToHex allocates a nibble slice of 2*len(path)+1 bytes for every path, then the trie is traversed with this oversized key. A malicious peer could send many requests with  large paths (up to the 10 MB message limit) to amplify memory allocation
````

#### Expected behaviour

HTTP virtual host validation should treat hostnames case-insensitively.

If `test` is present in the configured vhost allowlist, requests with `Host: test`,
`Host: TEST`, or `Host: TeSt:1234` should all be accepted.

#### Actual behaviour

The configured vhost allowlist is normalized to lowercase, but the incoming HTTP

As a result, a request with a mixed-case hostname such as `Host: TeSt:1234` is
rejected with:

```text
invalid host specified
```

This is a user-facing RPC issue because hostname matching is expected to be
case-insensitive.

#### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

1. Start geth with HTTP RPC enabled and a lowercase vhost allowlist entry, for example:


Currently, `UnpackXxxEvent` methods return signature mismatch errors defined inline via `errors.New("event signature mismatch")`. issues.title: core: txLookupLock mutex leaked on error returns in reorg()
Potential deadlock in reorg() due to unreleased txLookupLock on error paths
issues.body_excerpt:
In core/blockchain.go, the reorg function acquires a write lock via bc.txLookupLock.Lock(). However, several early return paths (specifically when bc.GetBlock returns nil) fail to call bc.txLookupLock.Unlock().

Lines leading to leak:

[Line 2651]: return errInvalidOldChain
[Line 2670]: return errInvalidOldChain
[Line 2685]: return errInvalidNewChain

This will cause any subsequent transaction lookups or further reorgs to hang indefinitely.

**Proposed Fix:**
Use defer bc.txLookupLock.Unlock() right after bc.txLookupLock.Lock() and remove the manual Unlock() at the end of the function to ensure the lock is always released.
